title: US wants Israel to 'crack down' on settler violence in West Bank, Rubio says
gist: Secretary of State Rubio said the US has asked Israel to crack down on West Bank settler violence after an attack on Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine; Yesh Din counts at least 170 settler attacks since Sept. 27.

themes.theme: US pressure on Israel over settler violence

insights.claim: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US has asked, and continues to ask, Israel to crack down on settler attacks in the West Bank.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Public US pressure on Israel over settlers could shape bilateral friction.
insights.quote: We've asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff.

insights.claim: Rubio expects to hear back from the US Embassy in Jerusalem by Sunday about the Friday incident, in which the State Department has made inquiries.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Follow-up findings may prompt further US statements.

insights.claim: Israeli settlers carried out at least 170 attacks on Palestinians since Sept. 27, around the start of the olive harvest, according to Yesh Din.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Persistent escalation during the harvest season raises international diplomatic costs for Israel.

insights.claim: Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was among at least two people injured in a Friday settler attack, and European diplomats and a French mayor were also attacked, per Belgium's foreign minister.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Attacks on Western nationals and diplomats widen the diplomatic fallout beyond the US.
